metadata.datasource: Characteristic curves, spectral sensitivities, dye spectra from W. I. Kisner, 'A New Color Negative Film for Better Picture Quality', Journal of the SMPTE 71(10), 1962, pp. 776-779, Figs. 1-3: EASTMAN Color Negative Film, Type 5251, integral density, taken as Status M; EI 50 tungsten and the 3200 K balance from Kodak's announcement in American Cinematographer, June 1962, pp. 362-363 and 385. The curves were traced off the paper's scan, levelled, each solid curve from a point on it with 5250's dashes taken out (kodak_1962_sheets.py), and converted from Status M densities into dye amounts. The sheet plots relative log exposure. Its exposure index, EI 50, is taken as its speed by the ASA/ISO method: the curves' ISO 5800 speed point (0.15 over D-min, green and slowest layer) at sqrt(2) / 50 lux-seconds; mid-grey goes at Kodak's normal exposure, 10/EI, 0.849 decades above. Past the sheet's last plotted exposure each curve continues at its final gradient for 0.8 decades (R 0.61, G 0.63, B 0.62), where the plot ends a few stops over normal and the film goes on. The sheet's sensitivity shapes continue on the donor's tails beyond the plotted range and are balanced so an 18% grey exposes every layer equally. No spectral adaptation window: agx fits one to each of its own stocks' sensitivities. No DIR couplers (stock_overrides.NO_COUPLERS). Base density from 'kodak_vision3_200t'.
